title.rendered: You Will Receive Power and Ability: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: You will receive power and ability. Jesus did not promise only access. He promised the equipping that comes with it. The same Spirit moves through your day.

content.rendered:
You will receive power and ability. Both. Jesus did not promise only access to the Spirit. He promised the equipping that comes with Him. The same Spirit who fell on Pentecost will move through your ordinary day today.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, May 22, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“But you will receive power and ability when the Holy Spirit comes upon you; and you will be My witnesses [to tell people about Me] both in Jerusalem and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the ends of the earth.”
Acts 1:8 (AMP)

Today’s Message

The Amplified Bible renders the Greek word dunamis in full: power and ability. Most English translations stop at “power.” But the original word holds both. The capacity and the capability. The inner strength and the outer skill. The fire and the wick it lights. Jesus did not just promise access to power. He promised the equipping to walk in it.

The proof came at Pentecost. The same Peter who had denied Jesus three times in front of a servant girl eight weeks earlier stood up that morning and preached the first sermon of the church. Three thousand people were saved that day. That was not Peter finally finding his confidence. That was Peter clothed with the Spirit and operating in ability he did not naturally possess.

Notice what Jesus said the power was for. “You will be My witnesses.” Not “you will have a great life.” Not “your problems will end.” The power that fell at Pentecost was missional power. The Spirit did not come down so the church could have warm feelings about Jesus. He came so His people could be sent.

Look at the geography in the verse: Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, the ends of the earth. Concentric circles widening outward. You start where you are. You move into the regions next to you. You cross over into territory you would not have entered in your own strength. And you keep going until the gospel reaches places that have not heard it yet.

This is not just for the pastors and the missionaries. Your workplace is your Jerusalem. Your family is your Judea. The stranger God puts in your path tomorrow is your Samaria. You are not exempt from this calling. You are equipped for it. The Spirit who fell on Peter is the Spirit who lives in you. The same dunamis. The same ability. The same Sender.

And here is where grace anchors the whole conversation: you are not generating the power. You are receiving it. “You will receive power and ability.” Receiving means it is given. The mission is His. The power is His. The fruit is His. You walk out the door today aware that the Spirit goes with you, in you, and through you. That is enough.

Prayer

Father, I receive Your power and ability today. I do not generate it. I do not earn it. I receive it as a gift through Jesus Christ. Send me as a witness wherever You have placed me. Let the Spirit move through me into the lives of those around me, in my Jerusalem and beyond. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I have received power and ability through the Holy Spirit. I am a witness wherever I go today—in my Jerusalem, in my Judea, in my Samaria. I am sent. The Spirit equips me. The gospel flows through me. The fruit belongs to Him.
